en: I pay homage to that Sugata,

the Tathāgata Vipashyin, the Teacher of the World, worshipped by the realms of gods and men, skilled in compassion, the instructor of supreme benefit and liberation, who has crossed over the flood of the great ocean of the three worlds. (1)
Having beheld the world sinking in this ocean of existence which has no further shore, he who revealed the Dharma for its welfare—to that Jina Śikhin, homage be! (2)

I pay homage to the Buddha, the source of the universe, whose splendor surpasses that of the moon and the sun, and who, like the unfathomable depth of the ocean's current, is immeasurable in wisdom and discipline. (3)
I pay homage to that great lord of sages, Kakupchanda, by whose glories— resembling the rays of the moon— this earth shines adorned, like a wondrous flower of the Udumbara tree.

I bow to that Kanakamuni, honored by the gods, by whom darkness was destroyed with a mind that is expansive, free from stain, dispassionate, and ever-acting for the welfare [of others]—a mind that is stainless. || 5 ||

I pay homage to the one named Kāśyapa, who is as fair as the radiance of molten gold, whose splendor and brilliance exceed a thousand suns, the supreme being in the world, and the one revered by all people.

Homage to that Teacher, the supremely compassionate Śākyamuni-lamp, who, having awakened the world with the net of rays of his speech— just as the sun awakens a cluster of lotuses with its rays of light— has now entered into final peace.
I bow with my whole being to him named Maitreya, who dwells in the abode of Tuṣita and whose enlightenment is indeed separated by only one birth; he who shall arise as a Sugata upon the earth.
Having praised the seven past Victors and the eighth Bodhisattva of the future, by whatever immeasurable merit has been acquired through this, may all sentient beings be free from affliction. (9)
